info.title: AI Operations Layer API
info.description:
The HTTP API of the AI Operations Layer collector: authenticated ingest of telemetry batches, and the permissioned query surface the console and every other client uses.

Telemetry is evidence, never authority: nothing the API returns may authorize a retry, refund or publication on its own, and gaps in the telemetry are shown as gaps, never as success.

Two credential kinds exist. An **ingest key** (`aiops_ik_…`) authorizes only `POST /v1/ingest`. An **API token** (`aiops_tk_…`) carries an actor, scopes (`read`, `operate`, `admin`) and a project list, and authorizes the query routes. Health probes are unauthenticated.

servers.description: A hosted collector (replace with your own origin)
The quick start on this machine

tags.name: ingest
tags.description: Batched telemetry from instrumented hosts, authenticated by ingest key.

tags.name: query
tags.description: The permissioned read surface, authenticated by API token.

tags.name: authority
tags.description: What the execution authority says about an operation — read live from the authority, never inferred from telemetry.

tags.name: control
tags.description: Safe, audited operator actions — reconcile and retry — where an adapter owns execution. Telemetry is never read to authorize them.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: The `admin`-scoped surface: the audit log and the credential inventory with revocation.

get.description: The process is alive. Answers `ok` without touching the store.
The store answers within one second. 200 when the collector can serve; 503 when PostgreSQL is unreachable.

post.description:
One batch: a `source` block naming the emitting instance, the instance's own drop counters in `stats`, and up to the configured maximum events.

Ingest is idempotent by `event_id`: a resent event counts as a duplicate, never a second event, and a duplicated event under a *different* operation is refused rather than merged. Individual events can be refused without failing the batch; refusals come back per index, never silently dropped. The whole batch is refused with an error status when the schema version is wrong, the body is malformed or too large, the key can't be read, or the key is rate-limited.

200.description: The batch was processed; per-event refusals are in `refused`.

400.description: Malformed body or unsupported schema version.

413.description: The batch exceeds the body limit or event-count limit.

429.description: The key's rate limiter refused the batch; retry after the `Retry-After` hint.

503.description: The collector shed the load or the store is unavailable.

get.summary: The token's actor, scopes and projects
get.description: Who the bearer token acts as, which scopes it holds, and which projects it may read. The console calls this first.

Operations in one project, newest first, from stored summaries — not raw events. Filter by status, name, request id, release or time window; page with `before_time`/`before_id` from the previous response's `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (bounded by the server's limits).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: RFC 3339: operations whose first event time is at or after it.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: RFC 3339: operations whose first event time is before it.

parameters.name: before_time
parameters.description: Pass back `next` for the next page.

400.description: A bad parameter (unknown status, overlong identifier, unparseable time).

403.description: The project isn't in the token's scope.

get.description: The full correlated view of one operation: declared status, flags, coverage (including known and unknown gaps), per-attempt steps, every stored entry, sources, cost estimates and retention state. Uncertainty is part of the payload — `no_finish_observed`, missing `op_seq` ranges, clock-skew and conflicting-finish flags are data, not errors.

403.description: The project isn't in the token's scope.

404.description: No operation by that id in this project.

get.description: Reads the configured execution authority (today: a Durable Runner deployment) live, after verifying that the named run derives to this operation. The answer is one of six explicit states — `answered`, `not_configured`, `not_linked`, `unknown_runner`, `link_unverified`, `unavailable` — so an authority that can't be reached is never silently replaced by a telemetry guess.

403.description: The project isn't in the token's scope.

404.description: No operation by that id in this project.

get.description: Up to four releases side by side over the same window, built from the same summaries and statuses the operations list uses. A release whose operations lost events or never finished shows that in its own columns — never as success. A release with no operations in the window is listed with zeros, never dropped.

parameters.name: releases
parameters.description: Comma-separated release names, at most four.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: RFC 3339 start of the window (the comparison caps at seven days).

400.description: Bad parameters (more than four releases, a window over seven days, unparseable times).

403.description: The project isn't in the token's scope.

get.description: The counters the collector keeps about itself: batches, accepted/duplicate/refused/conflicting events, withheld attributes and redactions, unauthenticated and denied calls, shed and rate-limited requests, store-unavailable count, and the in-process lock wait/hold times. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.summary: Reconcile an operation against the effect's authority
post.description: Reads the effect's own authority (never the telemetry) for `business_key` and stores the answer on a control record: `resolution` is `effect_present`, `effect_absent` or `still_uncertain`. Changes nothing outside the layer — safe to run before deciding anything. Requires the `operate` scope and a configured control adapter for the project.

400.description: Bad request (key format, `expected_state` shape, bad id).

403.description: Denied — scope missing, no adapter for the project, or unknown operation; the denial is audited.

409.description: `conflicting_request` — a record exists for this operation, action and key with a different `expected_state`.

503.description: Store or audit unavailable — the call was refused (denials fail closed).

post.summary: Retry an operation under its business key
post.description: Resubmits the operation's work through the host's public contract under the same business key — after the authority's own checks. Authorized only when the effect is confirmed absent and the caller's `expected_state` matches; an effect that already happened denies with `effect_confirmed` — the correct recovery for a landed effect is none. The decision, the authority snapshot and the audit row commit in one transaction; the external call happens only after, and its outcome is observed against the authority — never assumed. There is no generic 'run again'. Requires `operate` scope and a configured adapter.

200.description: The retry record — typically `authorized` or `denied` at return; the executor drives `submitted → confirmed | submit_failed | observed_unknown` afterwards.

409.description: `conflicting_request` on a replayed key with a different `expected_state`.

get.description: Every control record for one operation — reconciles, retries, their decisions and terminal states. A `read` scope call.

403.description: The project isn't in the token's scope (audited).

get.description: A single control record by id — the live status of a reconcile or retry drive. A `read` scope call.

404.description: No such control record on this operation.

get.description: The decision log, newest first, keyset-paged: token mints and revokes, control calls (authorized and denied — every denial is a decision and is recorded), scoped admin actions. **The read itself is never audited** — a read that wrote rows would grow the log on every page turn. Metadata only: actor, action, target, decision, reason, time; no secrets or bodies exist in the log. Requires `admin` scope; runs on the control pool so an incident read can't starve behind a query flood.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Filter to one action, e.g. `control.retry` or `admin.revoke_token`.

400.description: Bad parameters (`before_time` without `before_id`, unparseable times or uuid).

get.description: Projects, ingest keys and API tokens in one read — ids, names, actors, scopes, project lists, creation/expiry/revocation times. Metadata only; hashes and secrets are never served. An allowed read is not audited; a denial always is. Requires `admin` scope.

post.summary: Revoke an API token by id
post.description: Revokes the token and evicts its cached answer **now**: a revoked credential dies on its next presentation, not when the resolver's TTL runs out. Audited under `admin.revoke_token` — the grant or the denial of an unknown id, synchronously, before the answer. Requires `admin` scope.

404.description: Unknown or already-revoked credential (the denial is audited).

503.description: Audit unavailable — the call was refused (denials fail closed).

post.summary: Revoke an ingest key by id
post.description: Revokes the ingest key and evicts its cached answer immediately — the key dies on its next presentation. Audited under `admin.revoke_ingest_key`. Requires `admin` scope.

ingestKey.description: An ingest key (`aiops_ik_…`), scoped to one project and usable only for `POST /v1/ingest`. Printed once by `aiops-server admin create-ingest-key`.

apiToken.description: An API token (`aiops_tk_…`) with an actor, scopes (`read`, `operate`, `admin`) and a project list. Printed once by `aiops-server admin create-token`.

Error.description: The single error envelope every route returns: a machine-readable `code`, a readable `message`, and `request_id` when one was assigned. HTTP 409 refusals and 503 unavailability use the same shape.

Source.description: The emitting instance a batch speaks for.

instance_id.description: Stable id of this host instance; its `seq` numbering is per instance.

BatchStats.description: The instance's own drop counters — loss the SDK already knows about, reported rather than hidden.

WireEvent.description: One event in the versioned wire contract (`docs/INGEST_CONTRACT.md` in the product repository). Per type, only the listed fields may appear — anything else is refused `field_not_allowed`. `event_id`, `type`, `operation_id`, `seq`, `op_seq` and `event_time` are always present; the type's own required fields follow it.

event_id.description: 32 lowercase hex, unique per project; the same on every re-delivery (the dedup key).

type.description: The event's kind in the contract.

seq.description: ≥ 1, per source instance, in emission order; holes here are exact known gaps.

op_seq.description: ≥ 1, per operation within the instance; `0` only on `gap.reported`.

event_time.description: When the host says it happened (the second clock is the collector's receive time).

external_effect.description: The step may cause an outside-world effect; an uncertain finish on it is flagged.

outcome.description: Declared by the host, never inferred. Required on `operation.finished` and `step.finished`; `failed` takes `failure_class`, `uncertain` takes `uncertain_reason`.

error_message.description: Free text; secret-shaped substrings are replaced with `[redacted]` and counted.

cost_estimate.description: The host's cost estimate — labelled estimate, never a reconciled bill.

events_emitted.description: Required on `operation.finished`: how many events the host emitted for the operation (≥ `op_seq`).

dropped.description: Required on `gap.reported`: how many events were dropped (≥ 1).

attributes.description: Optional, ≤ 32 entries; policy-filtered on ingest — withheld counts, redactions and truncation stay visible.

truncated.description: How many string fields the sender cut to the caps.

schema_version.description: The wire contract version. A mismatch refuses the whole batch.

RefusedEvent.description: One event the collector refused; the rest of the batch still went on.

duplicates.description: Events already stored under the same `event_id` — idempotent resends, not new data.

withheld_attributes.description: Attribute keys the default-deny policy withheld, summed over the batch — attributes are opt-in per project; counted, never stored.

redactions.description: Secret-shaped strings replaced with `[redacted]` inside stored values, summed over the batch.

overflowed_names.description: Operation and step names over the project's or the key's cardinality budget; the events store under the `_overflow` name.

Status.description: The declared status: what the host's `operation.finished` said. `no_finish_observed` means exactly that — no finish was observed; it is never rendered as "running" or "did not run".

declared.description: Whether a finish event was observed at all.

events_missing.description: `emitted - received` when the finish arrived; otherwise unknown — never guessed.

detail_expired.description: Raw events older than the retention cutoff may be deleted; the summary still stands.

multi_source.description: Events came from several source instances; per-source completeness lives in the timeline.

next.description: Pass back as `before_time`/`before_id` for the next page; absent at the end.

external_effect_unknown.description: A step with `external_effect` finished uncertain or unobserved — an outside-world effect may have happened.

tail_unknown.description: The instance hasn't finished or gone silent after a declared end; what came after the last received event is unknown.

missing_unknown.description: Loss is possible beyond the known holes (an unfinished tail, an unreported drop).

CostView.description: Always an estimate, never a reconciled bill — the label is part of the payload.

opt_in.description: Included only because the project opted this key in.

EntryView.description: One stored event as the timeline renders it, with both clocks.

GapView.description: A stretch the timeline knows it's missing.

Timeline.description: One operation's correlated record: declared status, flags, coverage, steps, entries, gaps, sources and retention state.

effect_unknown_steps.description: Step ids whose uncertain or unobserved finish may hide an outside-world effect.

expired_by_retention.description: Stored events deleted by retention; their place in the timeline is still shown.

LockView.description: Wait and hold-time counters for one in-process lock.

RunView.description: The runner's own answer, verbatim — never re-derived from telemetry.

Authority.description: One of six explicit states, tagged by `state`. `unavailable` means the authority could not be asked or answered usably — nothing is inferred in its place.

ControlRequest.description: The operator's assertion. `business_key` names the effect's own key at the authority (for the reference host, `article:<id>`); `expected_state` is what the operator asserts the authority's state to be (for the reference host, exactly `{"published": bool}`). Replaying the same operation, action and business key with the same `expected_state` returns the existing record (`replayed: true`); a different `expected_state` is refused `409 conflicting_request`.

ControlView.description: One control record: the layer's authoritative record of one operator action. Status moves only forward: reconcile goes `reconciling → reconciled`; retry goes `requested → authorized|denied → submitted → confirmed | submit_failed | observed_unknown`. `denied` is terminal — a decision, not an absence.

resolution.description: On a reconcile record: what the authority answered. `still_uncertain` means it could not answer within the read bound — never guessed.

authority_read.description: The stored snapshot `{source, status, answer, read_at}` the decision was made from.

submitted_ref.description: The resubmitted work's own identity at the host — a new operation id, or the Durable Runner's new op_key ↔ business_key mapping.

replayed.description: `true` when a repeated call returned the existing record unchanged.

AuditEntryView.description: One audit row — metadata only; no secret, digest or request body is ever stored.

next.description: Pass back as `before_time`/`before_id` for the next page; absent on the last.

CredentialList.description: The whole credential surface — metadata only, no secrets or digests.
